changelog: [Never Segment]: replaced the general elided-predicate/coreferential-subject bullets with five sharper, positionally-specific conditions matching the measured wrong-boundary failures: (1) do not split a term from a later clause that restates/clarifies that same term's sense, (2) do not split a concessive clause from a following conditional clause whose verb/subject is elided and recoverable only from the concessive, (3) do not split a zero-subject clause away from a self-referential antecedent established two or more clauses earlier, (4) do not split between a clause that introduces an explicit subject and a later zero-subject clause that inherits its person/number even across an intervening connective, (5) do not split a zero-subject clause away from a later clause that identifies its subject via a pronoun or name. These state conditions, not banned connective forms, per the critic's boundary-placement evidence.

[Decision Procedure]: expanded step 2's checklist to explicitly test each of the five new conditions (ambiguous-term restatement, concessive→conditional elided dependency, multi-clause self-referential subject, cross-connective subject inheritance, deferred subject-identifying token) so the accept/reject test operationalizes the refined [Never Segment] conditions rather than only the older generic elided-predicate/coreference check.
